records.groupTitle: Average Number Of Children Born To Resident Ever-Married Females Aged 40-49 Years By Highest Qualification Attained (HQA)
records.title: Average Number Of Children Born To Resident Ever-Married Females Aged 40-49 Years By Highest Qualification Attained (HQA), Annual
records.footnote: Data by highest qualification attained pertain to residents who were not attending educational institutions as full-time students and include those who were upgrading their qualifications through part-time courses. Data for 1990, 2000, 2010 and 2020 are based on the Census of Population while data for 2005, 2015 and 2025 are based on the General Household Survey. Data for all other years are based on the Comprehensive June Labour Force Survey. Survey estimates are subject to sampling variability.

row.footnote: Further breakdown of the data into 'Below Secondary' and 'Secondary' for years 2024 & onwards are not shown as the survey-based data are subject to high sampling variability arising from small population groups. For example, as the educational profile of the Singapore resident population continues to improve, the proportion of resident ever-married females aged 40-49 years with Below Secondary qualification has fallen below 7 per cent in 2024 and is expected to decline further.
